title.en: Huo Qubing’s early campaign and enfeoffment

summary.en: The Shiji describes Huo Qubing as eighteen when he accompanied Wei Qing and led 800 light cavalry away from the main army. Its account reports killings and captures, followed by his enfeoffment as Marquis of Guanjun. The title follows the expedition; it is not a rank he already held when setting out.
summary.zh: 《史记》记霍去病“年十八”随卫青出征，率八百轻骑离开大军深入；继而记杀获与封冠军侯。封号在此次出征之后，并非出发时已有的爵位。

title.en: Hexi in 121 BCE: campaigns, surrender and resettlement
title.zh: 公元前121年的河西：征战、降附与迁徙

summary.en: The Shiji separates spring and summer campaigns from the autumn reception of Hunye’s people. Huo Qubing’s forces attacked through the western Xiongnu territories; during the later surrender, the text reports that 8,000 people attempting to leave were killed. Those who crossed into Han territory were subsequently moved into dependent communities along the frontier.
summary.zh: 《史记》将春夏征战与秋天接收浑邪王部众分开叙述。霍去病军进攻匈奴西部；后来的降附过程中，记有八千欲离去者被杀。渡河入汉的部众，随后被迁置边郡故塞外，设置属国。

summary.en: The Shiji places Huo Qubing’s march past Juyan toward the Qilian Mountains in the summer of 121 BCE. It reports captures and killings, while the imperial commendation also acknowledges that his army had been reduced by three-tenths. Hunye’s surrender follows in the autumn, rather than being part of the same summer encounter.
summary.zh: 《史记》将霍去病越居延、至祁连山的进军记在公元前121年夏季。传记记述杀获，所引诏书也称其军“减什三”。浑邪王降附则记在秋季，并非同一场夏季交战。

title.en: Mobei: two armies and a costly desert campaign
title.zh: 漠北：两支军队与高昂的远征代价

summary.en: The Shiji describes Wei Qing and Huo Qubing each leading 50,000 cavalry north of the desert in 119 BCE. Wei Qing encountered the chanyu, who escaped, while Huo Qubing advanced on a separate route. The account reports that fewer than 30,000 of the 140,000 horses taken beyond the frontier returned, making logistics and losses central to the campaign.
summary.zh: 《史记》记公元前119年卫青、霍去病各率五万骑越漠。卫青遭遇单于，单于突围而去；霍去病另路深入。传记称出塞官私马十四万匹，返回者不足三万，后勤与损耗构成此次远征的重要一面。

sources.evidenceNote: Lines 176–181: separate routes, chanyu’s escape and 140,000 horses out / fewer than 30,000 back. Numbers are attributed to the text.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 176—181行：两路进军、单于逃脱及出塞十四万马、归者不足三万；数字注明来自史书。

summary.en: The Shiji quotes an imperial commendation describing Huo Qubing’s northern advance, rites at Mount Langjuxu and Guyan, and arrival at Hanhai. The same passage reports both large captures and a reduction of three-tenths in his force. Ritual, reward and military accounting are presented together in the court’s record of victory.
summary.zh: 《史记》所引诏书叙述霍去病向北进军、封狼居胥山、禅姑衍，并登临翰海。同一段也记大量杀获与本军减什三；仪式、封赏与军功计算共同构成朝廷对胜利的记述。

sources.author: 司马迁 · Sima Qian
sources.evidenceNote: Line 180, imperial commendation: Langjuxu, Guyan and Hanhai, captures and three-tenths reduction. Does not assert a modern identification for these places.

context.en: The Western Han tomb sculpture commemorates Huo Qubing’s military career after his death. This 1914 photograph shows how that career was represented in stone.
context.zh: 西汉墓前石刻在霍去病死后纪念其军旅生涯。1914年的照片让读者观察这些功业如何被转化为石雕。

context.en: The horse above a fallen figure is a monument to victory. Read its commemorative language alongside the account of surrender, coercion and migration.
context.zh: 石马压在倒伏人形之上，以纪念物的语言表现胜利；可将它与降附、强制和迁徙的记载并读。

context.en: The stone horse belongs to Huo Qubing’s funerary commemoration. Its triumphant form contrasts with the text’s acknowledgment of losses during the campaign.
context.zh: 石马属于霍去病的陵墓纪念；其胜利形象可与文字中对战役损耗的承认相对照。

context.en: This monument commemorates one of the expedition’s commanders, Huo Qubing. Its victory imagery offers a counterpoint to the narrative’s material cost.
context.zh: 这件纪念物关联远征统帅之一霍去病。其胜利图像可与叙事中的物资代价并看。

context.en: The tomb sculpture and the quoted commendation are two forms of memorializing Huo Qubing’s achievements: one in stone, the other through ritual and rewards in the written record.
context.zh: 墓前石刻与所引诏书，是纪念霍去病功业的两种方式：一以石雕表现，一以文字中的仪式和封赏表达。
